verification_report.summary:
The mathematical adaptation and the new numerical proof pass verification. The overall submission receives the strict verdict wrong solely because the requested complete adaptation map contains one unresolved file-hash discrepancy.

The accepted source has the specified SHA256, and its files and transcendental_nakamaye_01 audit remain unchanged. The source proof was accepted as instructed. A complete substantive comparison, including edits made externally during this audit, found no changed formula or missing hypothesis beyond the declared changes. All 93 retained source labels have the nk: prefix; references resolve, bibliography identities are preserved, and operator expansions retain the source conventions. Removed front matter and the Setup replacement lose no mathematical premise.

The theorem preserves componentwise vanishing for positive-dimensional irreducible components and equality with the numerical null locus; it does not assert vanishing on every contained subvariety. Shared Kähler definitions agree, including smooth remainders in the restricted-volume supremum and image-ideal restriction. The existing no-isolated-locus proposition applies in the big-class branch. All three relative-principalization applications satisfy connectedness. The dependency table correctly permits the final modification and exceptional correction to depend on M.

The numerical criterion was checked deduction by deduction without assuming its conclusion. The curve case, fixed positive perturbation, choice of epsilon before the test form, both Stokes identities, exceptional-set estimate, eigenvalue bound and exact 4k constant are valid. The actual hypotheses of thm:tw-smooth and thm:lamari hold. Cancellation of the epsilon classes yields a positive current in A-B', and adding eta times the Kähler form proves bigness. ArXiv theorem search and the published [Xiao15 Theorem 1.4](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/aif.2959.pdf) confirm the attribution and definitions.

The main argument needs only the accepted original Kähler specializations of quantitative regularization and the global ideal potential lemma. No general Hermitian bounded mass property is assumed. The final Hermitian discussion remains conditional on hermitian_quantitative_regularization_01; this audit does not establish those generalizations. Both audits must pass before inclusion. Detailed checks and comparison evidence are preserved under this run.
